words.en: An employment agency is a business that helps people to find jobs and employers to find suitable workers.

words.ex: It was raining; nevertheless, we went for a walk.
words.ex_cn: 天下雨了；尽管如此，我们还是去散步了。
words.en: Despite what has just been said or done; nonetheless.

words.tr: phrase. v.平均下来：在一段时间内产生一个均衡的结果。; 总体上来说：总体来看，有时你赢，有时你输，最终一切都会...
words.ex: The prices average out to $10 each.
words.ex_cn: 这些价格平均下来是每件10美元。
words.en: To calculate the mean of numbers or amounts, or to reach a typical level or amount after various increases and decreases.

words.tr:
v. 抓住；持有；容纳；保留；举行；
n. 拿；控制；持；
words.ex: He held the rope tightly.
words.ex_cn: 他紧紧抓住了绳子。
words.en: To have or keep in the hand; to maintain in a grasp; to keep in a specified state, relation, or position; to contain or be capable of containing; to have in one's possession; to keep back from action; to delay the action or effect of; to keep in custody; to bear, sustain, or support; to have or maintain in the mind; to consider or esteem; to assert or affirm; to organize and carry on; to have the ownership or use of; to keep from falling or moving; to remain unbroken or unyielding; to remain attached or faithful; to remain valid or effective.

words.ex: He wants to study engineering at university.
words.ex_cn: 他想在大学学习工程。
words.en: Engineering is the work involved in designing and constructing engines and machinery, or structures such as roads and bridges. Engineering is also the subject studied by people who want to do this work.

words.tr:
adj. 专业的；职业的；
n. 专业人士；
words.ex: He is a professional teacher with many years of experience.
words.ex_cn: 他是一位有多年经验的专业教师。
words.en: A professional is a person who has a job that requires special training and education, especially one that involves a high level of skill or knowledge.

words.tr: phrase. 务必确保；负责使…发生（或完成）
words.ex: See to it that the door is locked.
words.ex_cn: 确保门锁好了。
words.en: To make sure that something is done or happens.

words.ex: The use of cyanide in gold mining is highly controversial.
words.ex_cn: 在金矿开采中使用氰化物引起了很大争议。
words.en: A highly toxic chemical compound that contains the group CN, consisting of a carbon atom triple-bonded to a nitrogen atom.

words.tr: phrase. 避开某事；不参与某事；不卷入某事
words.ex: It's better to stay out of their family disputes.
words.ex_cn: 最好不要参与他们的家庭纷争。
words.en: If you stay out of something, you do not get involved in it.

words.ex: The lawyer helped her client with the contract.
words.ex_cn: 律师帮助她的客户处理合同。
words.en: A client is a person or organization receiving services or advice from a professional or company.

words.tr: phrase. 电椅（用于执行死刑的一种设备）
words.ex: The electric chair was used as a method of execution in some states.
words.ex_cn: 在一些州，电刑椅被用作一种处决方式。
words.en: A chair equipped with electrodes for the execution of a condemned person by electrocution.

words.ex: His incompetence caused the project to fail.
words.ex_cn: 他的无能力导致项目失败。
words.en: If you refer to someone's incompetence, you are criticizing them because they are unable to do their job or a task properly.

words.ex: His pursuit of happiness made him work hard every day.
words.ex_cn: 他对幸福的追求让他每天努力工作。
words.en: The act of pursuing something or someone, especially in order to catch or achieve them.

words.tr:
n. 后部；
v. 饲养；抚养；
adj. 后面的；
words.ex: The rear of the car was damaged in the accident.
words.ex_cn: 汽车的后部在事故中受损了。
words.en: The back part of something, especially a building or vehicle; to bring up and care for a child until they are fully grown.

words.ex: One apple will suffice for now.
words.ex_cn: 一个苹果现在就足够了。
words.en: If something suffices, it is enough to achieve a purpose or to fulfill a need.

words.tr:
adj. 敏锐的；尖锐的；穿透的；有洞察力的
v. 渗透；看穿；洞察；“penetrate”的现在分词
words.ex: His penetrating eyes saw the truth immediately.
words.ex_cn: 他敏锐的目光立刻看出了真相。
words.en: Able to make a way through or into something; showing an ability to understand things clearly and deeply.

words.ex: People vote in democracy to choose their leaders.
words.ex_cn: 人们在民主制度下投票选择他们的领导人。
words.en: A system of government by the whole population or all the eligible members of a state, typically through elected representatives.

words.tr: v. 主持；指挥；担任会议主席
words.ex: He presides over the meeting every Monday.
words.ex_cn: 他每周一主持会议。
words.en: To preside means to be in charge of a formal meeting, ceremony, or other event.

words.ex: The continuity of the story made it easy to follow.
words.ex_cn: 这个故事的连续性让它容易理解。
words.en: Continuity is the fact that something continues to happen or exist, with no great changes or interruptions.

words.ex: He votes in a democratic election.
words.ex_cn: 他在民主选举中投票。
words.en: A democratic country, government, or political system is governed by representatives who are elected by the people.

words.ex: His intellect helps him solve difficult problems.
words.ex_cn: 他的智力帮助他解决难题。
words.en: The ability to understand and think in a logical way about things.

words.tr: adj. 敏感的；感情脆弱的；体贴的；善解人意的；
words.ex: He is sensitive to loud noises.
words.ex_cn: 他对大声响很敏感。
words.en: If you are sensitive to other people's needs, problems, or feelings, you understand and are aware of them.

words.ex: A shudder ran through her when she saw the snake.
words.ex_cn: 当她看到蛇时，全身战栗了一下。
words.en: If you shudder, you shake with fear, horror, or disgust, or because you are cold.

words.ex: The farmer tried to kill the pest with a spray.
words.ex_cn: 农民试图用喷雾杀死害虫。
words.en: A pest is an animal or insect that damages crops, food, or livestock, or is generally troublesome. It can also refer to a person or thing that causes annoyance or trouble.

words.tr: adj. 卡住的；受困的； v. 粘贴；“stick”的过去式和过去分词；
words.ex: The door is stuck and won't open.
words.ex_cn: 门卡住了，打不开。
words.en: If something is stuck in a particular position, it is fixed tightly in this position and is unable to move.

words.tr: phrase. 美术；纯艺术（如绘画、雕塑、音乐、舞蹈等）
words.ex: He loves painting in the fine arts class.
words.ex_cn: 他喜欢在美术课上画画。
words.en: The term 'fine arts' refers to art forms developed primarily for aesthetics and/or concept rather than utility.

words.tr: phrase. 没有权利做某事；不该做某事
words.ex: You have no business telling me how to live my life.
words.ex_cn: 你没有权利告诉我如何生活。
words.en: If you say that someone has no business to do something, you mean that they have no right to do it.

words.ex: This forest has many different species of birds.
words.ex_cn: 这片森林有多种不同的鸟类物种。
words.en: A species is a class of plants or animals whose members have the same main characteristics and are able to breed with each other.

words.ex: The factory will mechanize its production line next year.
words.ex_cn: 这家工厂明年将使生产线实现机械化。
words.en: To mechanize something means to change it so that it is done by machines or mechanical processes rather than by human labor.

words.ex: The savage wolf howled under the moon.
words.ex_cn: 那头野性的狼在月光下嚎叫。
words.en: A savage person or animal is very fierce and violent.

words.tr: adj. 按键; 按钮操作的
words.ex: The new model features push-button ignition.
words.ex_cn: 新型号具有按键启动功能。
words.en: A push-button system or machine is operated by pressing buttons rather than by using more traditional controls.

words.ex: The cave had a neanderthal tool inside.
words.ex_cn: 洞穴里有一件尼安德特人的工具。
words.en: Neanderthal refers to an extinct species of human that was widely distributed in ice-age Europe between c. 120,000–35,000 years ago, with a receding forehead and prominent brow ridges. The term is also used to describe something that is primitive or uncivilized.

words.tr: phrase. 生命形式；生物体；活物
words.ex: The planet is believed to host a variety of life forms.
words.ex_cn: 人们相信这个星球上有多种生命形态。
words.en: A life form is any living thing, such as a plant, animal, or microorganism, that is capable of growth, reproduction, and response to stimuli.

words.tr: adj. 未受协助的；独立的；
words.ex: He solved the puzzle unaided.
words.ex_cn: 他未受协助地解开了这个谜题。
words.en: Without help from anyone or anything.

words.ex: This town has a peculiar custom of dancing at midnight.
words.ex_cn: 这个小镇有一个独特的午夜跳舞习俗。
words.en: If you describe someone or something as peculiar, you think that they are strange or unusual, sometimes in an unpleasant way.

words.ex: The glass broke into small fragments.
words.ex_cn: 玻璃碎成了小碎片。
words.en: A fragment of something is a small piece or part of it.

words.ex: He took his words in a literal sense.
words.ex_cn: 他把他的话按字面意思理解。
words.en: If you describe something as the literal truth or a literal fact, you are emphasizing that it is true.

words.ex: In essence, he is a kind person.
words.ex_cn: 本质上，他是一个善良的人。
words.en: You use in essence to emphasize that you are talking about the most important or central aspect of an idea, situation, or event.

words.ex: He behaved arrogantly towards his subordinates.
words.ex_cn: 他对下属表现得非常傲慢。
words.en: In a manner that shows an offensive attitude of superiority.

words.tr: n. 人性；人类；人道；仁慈；
words.ex: Kindness shows the best of humanity.
words.ex_cn: 善良展现了人性中最美好的一面。
words.en: Humanity refers to all human beings collectively or the qualities that make us human, such as kindness, compassion, and the ability to reason.

words.ex: He was charged with manslaughter after the car accident.
words.ex_cn: 他在车祸后被指控过失杀人。
words.en: Manslaughter is the crime of killing a person when the killer did not intend to do it or cannot be responsible for their actions at the time.

words.ex: The company is a legal entity.
words.ex_cn: 这家公司是一个法律实体。
words.en: An entity is something that exists separately from other things and has a clear identity of its own.

words.tr: phrase. 文科；人文科学（包括语言、哲学、历史、文学、艺术等学科）
words.ex: He majors in liberal arts at university.
words.ex_cn: 他在大学主修文科。
words.en: The liberal arts are academic subjects such as history, literature, and languages, as distinct from professional and technical subjects.

words.tr: adv. 含蓄地；暗中地；隐含地
words.ex: She implied her disappointment implicitly.
words.ex_cn: 她含蓄地表达了她的失望。
words.en: In a way that is not directly expressed but is understood or implied.

words.ex: The farm has a big storehouse for grain.
words.ex_cn: 这个农场有一个存放谷物的大仓库。
words.en: A storehouse is a building where things are stored.

words.ex: He felt culture shock when he moved to Japan.
words.ex_cn: 当他搬到日本时，他感受到了文化冲击。
words.en: Culture shock is the feeling of disorientation experienced by someone when they are suddenly subjected to an unfamiliar culture, way of life, or set of attitudes.

words.tr:
v. 移栽；移植；
n. 移植；
words.ex: He will transplant the flowers to the garden tomorrow.
words.ex_cn: 他明天要把这些花移栽到花园里。
words.en: To transplant something means to move it from one place to another. In medicine, to transplant an organ, piece of skin, etc. means to use it to replace a damaged part in someone's body.

words.ex: He went abroad to study medicine.
words.ex_cn: 他去国外学医。
words.en: In or to a foreign country or countries.

words.ex: He had a minor ailment and stayed home from work.
words.ex_cn: 他得了一点小病，没去上班。
words.en: An ailment is a minor illness or health problem.

words.ex: He has a high fever as a symptom of the flu.
words.ex_cn: 他发烧是流感的症状。
words.en: A symptom is a physical or mental feature which is regarded as indicating a condition of disease, particularly such a feature that is apparent to the patient.

words.tr:
v. 加速（坏事的发生）
n. 沉淀物；冷凝物
adj. 轻率的；仓促的
words.ex: The scandal precipitated the politician's resignation.
words.ex_cn: 这起丑闻加速了这位政治家的辞职。
words.en: To cause something to happen suddenly or unexpectedly; to cause a substance to be deposited in solid form from a solution.

words.tr:
n. 结果；
v. 导致；
words.ex: The result of the test was good.
words.ex_cn: 这次测试的结果很好。
words.en: A consequence, outcome, or effect of an action or situation.

words.ex: There is little intercourse between the two villages.
words.ex_cn: 这两个村庄之间很少交往。
words.en: Intercourse refers to communication or dealings between individuals or groups, or sexual activity between people.

words.ex: He used the sun to orient himself.
words.ex_cn: 他用太阳来确定方向。
words.en: To orient means to align or position something in relation to the points of a compass or other specified positions, or to familiarize someone with a new situation or environment.

words.tr: phrase. 使自己熟悉环境：通过观察和了解周围环境，使自己适应并熟悉新环境。
words.ex: He looked at the map to orient himself in the new city.
words.ex_cn: 他看着地图，以便在新城市中确定自己的方位。
words.en: To familiarize (someone) with new surroundings or circumstances.

words.tr: phrase. 形容某人处于不适应或不舒服的环境中，就像鱼离开了水一样
words.ex: At the tech conference, she felt like a fish out of water among all the programmers.
words.ex_cn: 在技术会议上，她在所有程序员中感觉像个不得其所的人。
words.en: Someone who is in a situation they are unsuited to, often feeling awkward or uncomfortable because they are different from the people around them.

words.ex: He is broad-minded and accepts different opinions.
words.ex_cn: 他思想开明，接受不同的观点。
words.en: Willing to respect or accept behavior or opinions different from one's own; open to new ideas.

words.ex: He watched the whole series of the show.
words.ex_cn: 他看完了这部剧的整个系列。
words.en: A series of things or events is a number of them that come one after the other.

words.tr:
n. 支撑物；支柱；道具
v. 支撑；靠
words.ex: He uses a prop to support the shelf.
words.ex_cn: 他用一个道具来支撑架子。
words.en: A prop is an object or piece of furniture that is used in a play or film to make a scene look more realistic, or something that is used to support or hold up another object.

words.ex: He reject the job offer.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝了这份工作邀请。
words.en: If you reject something such as a proposal, a request, or an offer, you do not accept it or you do not agree to it.

words.ex: The regression of the society was caused by war and poverty.
words.ex_cn: 社会的倒退是由战争和贫困造成的。
words.en: Regression is a statistical method used to examine the relationship between two or more variables. In a broader sense, it refers to the process of returning to a former or less developed state.

words.ex: The earthquake caused tremendous damage.
words.ex_cn: 地震造成了巨大的破坏。
words.en: If you describe something or someone as tremendous, you mean that they are very great in amount, extent, or intensity.

words.tr: adv. 无理性地；不合理地；
words.ex: He reacted irrationally to the small problem.
words.ex_cn: 他对这个小问题无理性地做出了反应。
words.en: In a manner that is not based on reason or clear thinking.

words.ex: The movie glorifies violence as heroism.
words.ex_cn: 这部电影美化了暴力，将其视为英雄主义。
words.en: To glorify someone or something means to praise them or make them seem more important or better than they really are.

words.ex: He got over his cold last week.
words.ex_cn: 他上周康复了。
words.en: To recover from something, such as an illness or a shock; to overcome a problem or difficulty.

words.ex: The weather can dictate what we wear each day.
words.ex_cn: 天气可以支配我们每天穿什么。
words.en: To dictate means to say or read something aloud for someone else to write down, or to give orders in an authoritative manner.

words.ex: He uses chopsticks to eat rice.
words.ex_cn: 他用筷子吃米饭。
words.en: A chopstick is one of a pair of thin sticks that are used for eating, especially in East Asia.

words.ex: The radio transmits music to listeners.
words.ex_cn: 收音机将音乐传递给听众。
words.en: To send or pass something from one person, place, or thing to another.

words.tr: phrase. 建立；逐步增长；加强
words.ex: He builds up his strength by running every day.
words.ex_cn: 他通过每天跑步来增强体力。
words.en: To increase or develop something gradually; to accumulate or amass something over time.

words.ex: He cleaned the floor by means of a mop.
words.ex_cn: 他用拖把打扫了地板。
words.en: If you do something by means of a particular method, instrument, or process, you do it using that method, instrument, or process.

words.ex: His explanation was understandable.
words.ex_cn: 他的解释是可以理解的。
words.en: If you describe someone's behaviour or feelings as understandable, you mean that they have reacted to a situation in a natural way or in the way you would expect.

words.tr: n. 民族优越感；本国中心主义
words.ex: Ethnocentrism often leads to misunderstandings and conflicts between different cultures.
words.ex_cn: 民族优越感常常导致不同文化之间的误解和冲突。
words.en: The belief in the inherent superiority of one's own ethnic group or culture.

words.tr: phrase. 与某人产生共鸣；把自己视为与某人同一阵线；认同某人
words.ex: She likes to identify herself with successful people.
words.ex_cn: 她喜欢与成功人士保持一致。
words.en: To associate oneself closely with someone or something; to feel a strong affinity or sympathy towards someone or something.

words.ex: He can identify the bird by its song.
words.ex_cn: 他能通过鸟的叫声识别它。
words.en: If you can identify someone or something, you are able to recognize them or distinguish them from others.

words.tr: phrase. 与…产生共鸣；把自己等同于…；认同某事物
words.ex: He refused to identify himself with the extremist group.
words.ex_cn: 他拒绝与极端组织有联系。
words.en: To consider oneself to be part of a particular group or movement, or to feel a strong connection with it.

words.tr: phrase. 与某人/某事物产生共鸣；认同某人/某事物；把自己与某人/某事物等同起来
words.ex: Many readers identify with the main character in the novel.
words.ex_cn: 许多读者对小说中的主角产生了共鸣。
words.en: To feel that you can understand and share the feelings of someone else.

words.ex: There is a tendency for people to use phones before bed.
words.ex_cn: 人们在睡觉前使用手机是一种趋势。
words.en: A tendency is a likelihood of behaving in a particular way or going in a particular direction, which is often bad or undesirable.

words.tr: n. 特性；怪癖；奇异之物
words.ex: One peculiarity of the old house is its red door.
words.ex_cn: 这座老房子的一个特点是它的红门。
words.en: A peculiarity is a characteristic or quality that is distinctive or unique to a particular person, place, or thing.

words.tr: adj. 反社会的；危害社会的；厌恶社交的；不合群的
words.ex: He is antisocial and rarely talks to others.
words.ex_cn: 他性格孤僻，很少与别人交谈。
words.en: If you describe someone's behavior as antisocial, you mean that it shows an unwillingness to associate with or be friendly with other people.

words.tr:
v. 谴责；责难；指责
n. 谴责；责难；指责
words.ex: The teacher censured the student for cheating.
words.ex_cn: 老师谴责了那个作弊的学生。
words.en: If you censure someone for something that they have done, you tell them that you strongly disapprove of it.

words.ex: The national flag flies high every morning.
words.ex_cn: 每天早上国旗都高高飘扬。
words.en: relating to or characteristic of a nation; common to a whole nation

words.tr: phrase. 进入；包括；参与；成为...一部分
words.ex: He will enter into the room after knocking.
words.ex_cn: 他敲门后会进入房间。
words.en: To begin or become involved in an activity, agreement, or condition.

words.ex: There was clear hostility between the two neighbors.
words.ex_cn: 两个邻居之间明显存在敌意。
words.en: Hostility is unfriendly or aggressive behaviour towards people or ideas.

words.ex: The maid cleans the house every morning.
words.ex_cn: 女仆每天早上打扫房子。
words.en: A maid is a woman who works as a servant in a hotel or in someone's home.

words.tr: phrase. 畅所欲言；打开；开放
words.ex: Please open up and tell me how you really feel.
words.ex_cn: 请畅所欲言，告诉我你真正的感受。
words.en: To make something available or accessible; to start or begin something.

words.ex: He habitually wakes up at 6 a.m.
words.ex_cn: 他习惯每天早上六点起床。
words.en: If someone does something habitually, they do it regularly or as a habit.

words.ex: The teacher will allocate books to students.
words.ex_cn: 老师将给学生分配书籍。
words.en: To allocate something means to give it to a particular person or use it for a particular purpose.

words.ex: Each participant must sign the form.
words.ex_cn: 每个参与者都必须签署表格。
words.en: A participant is someone who takes part in an activity or event.

words.ex: We went to the carnival last weekend.
words.ex_cn: 我们上周末去了嘉年华。
words.en: A carnival is a public festival, typically one held annually in a particular place, involving processions, music, and dancing.

words.tr: n. （宗教等的）仪式；例行习惯；
words.ex: The village holds a ritual every spring to pray for good weather.
words.ex_cn: 这个村庄每年春天都举行一个仪式，祈求好天气。
words.en: A ritual is a religious service or other ceremony which involves a series of actions performed in a fixed order.

words.ex: He is a teacher, and as such, he must be patient.
words.ex_cn: 他是一名老师，同样地，他必须有耐心。
words.en: You use as such after a noun to indicate that you are considering that thing on its own, separately from other things.

words.tr: phrase. 角色扮演( role play的现在分词 )
words.ex: Role playing is a common technique used in training sessions.
words.ex_cn: 角色扮演是培训课程中常用的一种技巧。
words.en: Role playing is the act of imitating the character and behavior of someone who is different from yourself, for example as a training exercise.
